Use of preferred overseas destinations, preferred languages, preferred fields of study and the preferred 25+ week duration
Academic preparation, adaptability, flexibility and maturity; selection preference for veterans of the U.S. armed forces when other factors are equal

official.application_route: Online application at apply.iie.org via the Boren Awards Apply Now page, before the national deadline and any earlier campus deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline; study in an overseas destination of which the applicant is not a citizen, outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

official.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests.
official.region: Worldwide - preferred destinations in Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America and the Middle East; Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are always ineligible.
official.program_type: Federal overseas study and research scholarship (National Security Education Program, DLNSEO)
official.english_requirement: No minimum language proficiency requirement for most languages; French and Spanish require intermediate-high (ILR 1+ or greater in Speaking; ILR 1 for STEM fields in the specified cases), and any French or Spanish award is made contingent on verification through testing.

applicant_utility.summary: Boren is a service-linked study-abroad grant rather than a general scholarship, so everything hinges on a credible national-security argument for your language and destination plus a concrete plan for the one-year federal service obligation. Target the $25,000 tier by designing a programme of at least 25 weeks that keeps 15-20 weekly classroom language hours at its core; shorter stays pay strictly less and duration bands are never rounded up. Budget against the eligible-cost list: the grant covers approved tuition, housing and food, Fly America airfare, insurance and visa costs, while passports, medical costs, a personal laptop, dependents and personal travel stay on you. Engage your campus representative early, because many campuses run internal deadlines that fall weeks before the January national deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizen undergraduates and graduate students who are certain about a federal national-security career and can accept a one-year federal service obligation after graduation.
application_readiness_checklist: Find out whether your institution has a Boren campus representative and an internal deadline, and plan around the earlier of the two dates.
Map your proposed programme against the preferred language, destination and duration lists (25+ weeks) before locking in a provider.
Line up referees early and share essay drafts with them before the January deadline.
Check the French/Spanish proficiency rules if either is your target language, and keep testing verification in mind.
Prepare a signed matriculation form or a dean/registrar letter proving you will still be enrolled when the programme ends.
If you are a Fellow proposing research or internships abroad, request host affiliation letters now rather than later.
common_rejection_risks: A weak or generic national-security rationale for the chosen language and destination.
Proposing a programme shorter than the preferred 25 weeks without a compelling justification.
Letting English-taught coursework dominate a programme that must keep 15-20 weekly language hours at its core.
Failing to show a realistic, specific path to the one-year federal service requirement.
Missing a campus internal deadline while focused on the national one.
Ignoring destination restrictions (Western Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand) or an approved-destination asterisk without naming a viable backup.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Passport fees, medical expenses including inoculations, copays, treatment, prescriptions and COVID testing, a personal laptop, dependent expenses, personal travel and entertainment, and U.S.-side personal costs such as car payments, student loan payments, personal taxes or U.S. housing.
document_audit: Programme selections made in the application can only be adjusted within the same language and country at roughly the same weekly language intensity.
Recommendations must come from referees named in your application, so brief them before your essays are final.
Fellows attaching research, internship or extra coursework need host affiliation letters to make the plan credible.
Arabic, Mandarin or Russian proposals in starred destinations must include a viable alternate programme in an unrestricted destination.
Home-institution matriculation fees are capped at $2,500 per semester ($5,000 overall) - check whether your programme charges more.
Keep proof of any other aid you receive; overlapping support reduces your Boren award dollar for dollar.
alerts: Duration bands are firm: 24 weeks plus a few days does not round up to the 25-week/$25,000 award.
Funding for programme expenses after 31 May 2028 is contingent on availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.
Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are permanently ineligible destinations.
Study tours of several countries, such as a semester at sea, are not eligible for funding.
Other financial aid applied to the same costs must be reported and may reduce the grant; student loans will not.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online application at apply.iie.org, submit by the national deadline (Fellowships 20 January 2027; Scholarships 27 January 2027, 5pm Eastern) plus any earlier campus deadline, and expect selection news in mid-to-late April.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50% tuition waiver, not a full ride, so you must fund the remaining USD 30,972 of tuition plus mandatory fees, health insurance, books, visa costs, flights and DC living costs yourself; secure that money before you invest in an application. Admission comes first: the scholarship letter of consideration is only issued after AUWCL admits you, which makes the AUWCL admission deadline the real gate, and it differs by modality (residential 1 November, hybrid/online 30 November for Spring 2027). The award carries a return-home commitment for at least the length of the scholarship and a 3.0/4.0 GPA floor, and breaching either can trigger repayment of the full award value. If funding is the barrier, the announcement itself points to the separate OAS Rowe Fund interest-free loans of up to USD 15,000.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Law graduates and practising lawyers from OAS member states (outside the US) who need an American LL.M. in human rights, humanitarian law or international arbitration and can cover the other half of tuition plus living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for AUWCL admission first - scholarship consideration only starts once the Admissions Letter is issued.
Prepare law-degree credentials and, for English programmes, English proficiency evidence well before 1 or 30 November 2026.
Build a full budget: remaining 50% tuition, mandatory fees, health insurance, books, visa, flights and Washington, D.C. living costs.
Shape your essay around concrete impact on return to your country of origin - it is an explicit selection criterion.
Argentine applicants: file the required form with the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina without waiting for the deadline.
Decide the modality early: residential, hybrid and online tracks have different deadlines, and only the English programmes can be taken onsite.
common_rejection_risks: Treating the scholarship as a separate application instead of an automatic consequence of AUWCL admission.
Missing the modality-specific deadline (residential 1 November versus hybrid/online 30 November 2026).
An essay that fails to make a credible, specific case for impact on return to the country of origin.
Being a current OAS scholarship holder, a US citizen or permanent resident, GS/OAS staff, consultant or relative, or an OAS Permanent official or relative.
Dropping below a 3.0/4.0 GPA, which forfeits the scholarship.
Declining the award after the programme start date without proof of force majeure, which can force full reimbursement.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of tuition (USD 30,972), mandatory university fees, round-trip travel, books and study materials, health insurance, graduation expenses, visa expenses, and all other living and study costs.
document_audit: The Admissions Letter is issued only after admission, so assemble AUWCL's requested documents before you apply rather than after.
Only the documents AUWCL requests go with the admission application; the scholarship decision rides on that admission file.
The Spanish-language LL.M. needs no English proficiency evidence - do not pay for tests you do not need.
Signing the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form is mandatory for the award to be formally granted.
The published tuition is the 2026-2027 price (USD 2,581 per credit, expected to rise 3-5% annually), so re-check the current total before budgeting.
The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel the announcement at any point during the process.
alerts: Tuition is expected to increase 3-5% each academic year, so the USD 61,944 total and USD 30,972 balance are 2026-2027 figures only.
The return-to-country commitment lasts at least as long as the scholarship; failure to comply can trigger reimbursement of the total scholarship value.
Scholarship benefits are conditional on academic performance and availability of funds.
Unsuccessful applicants are not contacted; results are published in August and December at www.oas.org/scholarships.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for AUWCL admission by the modality deadline (residential 1 November 2026; hybrid/online 30 November 2026 for Spring 2027), receive the Admissions Letter, then await the joint AUWCL-OAS selection with results published in August and December.
